primitives.name: Hawkes Process
primitives.verbatim_quote: We investigate the timing of threat events and ball touches of players, and capture their correlation using Hawkes processes.
primitives.assumptions: The intensity of a player's ball touches depends on the history of all players' touches, modeled as a self-exciting point process.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When interaction kernels decay too rapidly, the Hawkes process reduces to independent Poisson processes, losing memory of collective behavior.

layer2.mapping: Maps Hawkes interaction history to GSI player contribution scores and GSE tactical state transitions.

primitives.name: Generation of Threat (GoT)
primitives.verbatim_quote: We define a new index, called _Generation of Threat_ (GoT), that measures in an unbiased way the contribution of a player to threat generation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Threats per touch (dimensionless), Threats per 90 minutes (min⁻¹).
primitives.assumptions: A player's contribution is proportional to the increase in hazard rate of threat arrival when they touch the ball, accounting for teammates' prior actions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when the underlying Hawkes network becomes disconnected, rendering the index non-invertible.

layer2.mapping: Equates GoT with posterior predictive threat counts under a conformalized Hawkes model, linking to GSI uncertainty quantification.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior variance of GoT estimates across cross-validation folds.

primitives.name: Direct and Indirect GoT
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our analysis reveals surprising results, with players such as Jason Berthomier, Moses Simon and Frederic Guilbert among the top performers in the GoT rankings.
primitives.assumptions: Direct GoT credits immediate ball receipt in the danger zone; indirect GoT accounts for cascading touches initiated by the player, weighted by interaction kernels $g_{ij}$.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Indirect GoT diverges when feedback loops dominate, causing supercritical branching ratios.

layer2.mapping: Decomposes total threat flow into direct vs. routed components, informing GSE routing efficiency metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of indirect to direct GoT coefficients, indicating team coordination depth.
